content: qui (which) is a discursive marker because it connects two ideas. The first one, “Avignon City is the capital of Vaucluse” (La ville d'Avignon est la capitale du Vaucluse), and the second one (satellite), “[Vaucluse] is a department in the south of France” ([Vaucluse] est un département du sud de la France). Several research has addressed automatic segmentation in several languages, such as: French BIBREF4, English BIBREF5, Portuguese BIBREF6, Spanish BIBREF7, BIBREF8 and Tahi. BIBREF9. All converge to the idea of using an explicit list of marks in order to segment texts.
